p.src: Now, when Jia Lian heard Xifeng say that she had something to discuss with him, he stopped and asked what it was. Xifeng said, “The twenty-first is Cousin Xue’s birthday. What do you think we should do about it?” Jia Lian replied, “How should I know what to do? You have arranged any number of grand birthday celebrations, yet now you are suddenly at a loss?” Xifeng said, “For grand birthdays, there are established rules to follow. But this birthday is neither a grand one nor an ordinary one, so I wanted to consult you.” Jia Lian listened, lowered his head, and thought for a long while before saying, “You are muddleheaded today. There is already a precedent: Cousin Lin’s celebration. Just celebrate Cousin Xue’s birthday this year in the same way you celebrated Cousin Lin’s in years past.” Xifeng gave a cold laugh. “Do you imagine I do not even know that? That was precisely what I had decided to do. But yesterday I heard the Old Lady asking everyone’s ages and birthdays. When she learned that eldest Cousin Xue turns fifteen this year, she said that although it is not a major birthday, it is still the age when a girl approaches her hairpin ceremony. The Old Lady said she wished to hold a birthday celebration for her. If she really does hold one for her, I should think it will naturally have to differ from Cousin Lin’s celebrations in former years.” Jia Lian said, “In that case, add a little more than was spent on Cousin Lin.” Xifeng said, “That was my thought too, which is why I wanted your opinion. If I added things on my own, you would blame me again for not explaining it clearly to you.” Jia Lian laughed. “Enough, enough! I want none of such empty favors. It is enough if you do not interrogate me about my affairs—how could I dare blame you?” With that, he went straight on his way, and nothing more need be said of it.

p.src: Meanwhile, after Shi Xiangyun had stayed for two days, she wanted to return home. Grandmother Jia said, “Wait until after your Cousin Bao’s birthday, and go home once you have seen the opera.” On hearing this, Shi Xiangyun had no choice but to remain. At the same time, she sent someone home to fetch two pieces of needlework she had made earlier, to present as birthday gifts to Baochai.

p.src: As it happened, ever since Baochai’s arrival, Grandmother Jia had been fond of her for her composed and gentle nature. Since this was the first birthday she had celebrated in the household, Grandmother Jia contributed twenty taels of her own money, summoned Xifeng, and entrusted her with arranging the feast and opera. Joining in the fun, Xifeng laughed and said, “When the venerable ancestress holds a birthday celebration for one of the children, no matter how it is done, who would dare object? Why even speak of arranging a feast and opera? If you are in the mood for merrymaking, you can hardly avoid spending a few taels of your own. Yet you have gone to all this trouble to dig out these moldy old twenty taels to play the host, meaning that I am expected to make up the balance. It would be another matter if you truly had no money, but gold and silver, round pieces and flat ones, are weighing down the bottoms of your chests, and still you stint us. Just look around—who here is not your child or grandchild? Can it be that in the end only Brother Bao will carry you up Mount Wutai? You mean to save all your private hoard for him. Though we may be unworthy of using it now, you need not make us suffer. Will this be enough for the wine? Will it be enough for the opera?” Her words set everyone in the room laughing. Grandmother Jia laughed too. “Just listen to that tongue of hers! I consider myself a good talker, yet even I cannot outtalk this monkey. Even your mother-in-law would not dare talk back, yet you keep wrangling with me.” Xifeng laughed. “My mother-in-law dotes on Baoyu just the same. I have nowhere to take my grievance, yet you accuse me of talking back.” With these words she made Grandmother Jia laugh again, and the old lady was delighted. That evening, after everyone had paid their evening respects before Grandmother Jia and the ladies and girls were chatting and laughing together, Grandmother Jia asked Baochai what operas she liked and what foods she enjoyed. Baochai knew well that Grandmother Jia was elderly, enjoyed lively operas, and favored sweet, soft foods, so she named only those things that the old lady had always liked. Grandmother Jia was more delighted than ever. The next day she sent over gifts of clothes, playthings, and other articles. Lady Wang, Xifeng, Daiyu, and the others all gave presents according to their means, each differing from the next, but there is no need to record them in detail. On the twenty-first, a small, informal stage was erected in Grandmother Jia’s inner courtyard, and a troupe was engaged to perform a selection of newly popular short pieces in both the Kunshan and Yiyang styles. Several tables for a family feast were laid in Grandmother Jia’s main apartments. There was not a single outsider present: only Aunt Xue, Shi Xiangyun, and Baochai counted as guests, while all the rest were members of the household. Early that morning, when Baoyu did not see Lin Daiyu, he went to her room to look for her and found her reclining on the kang. Baoyu said with a smile, “Get up and come eat. The opera is about to begin. Which piece would you like to see? Then I can request it.” Lin Daiyu gave a cold laugh. “If that is what you mean, then engage a troupe especially for me and have them perform whatever I like. There is no need to presume upon someone else’s celebration now and ask me merely so I may share in its reflected glory.” Baoyu laughed. “There is nothing difficult about that. We shall do exactly that tomorrow and let them share in our celebration for a change.”

p.src: After the meal, when it was time to choose the operas, Grandmother Jia insisted that Baochai choose first. Baochai politely declined once, but finding no way out of it, she chose a scene from Journey to the West. Grandmother Jia was naturally delighted, and then told Xifeng to choose. Xifeng knew that Grandmother Jia enjoyed lively performances, especially comic banter and clowning, so she chose Liu Er Pawns His Clothes. Grandmother Jia was even more pleased, just as expected, and then asked Daiyu to choose. Daiyu deferred to Aunt Xue, Lady Wang, and the others. Grandmother Jia said, “Today I specially brought you girls along to enjoy yourselves. We need only please ourselves and pay no attention to them. Do you suppose I went to all this trouble of arranging operas and a feast for their sake? They are already getting a fine bargain, watching and eating here for nothing—must we let them choose the plays as well?” At this, everyone laughed. Only then did Daiyu choose a piece. After her, Baoyu, Shi Xiangyun, Yingchun, Tanchun, Xichun, Li Wan, and the rest each made a choice, and the pieces were performed one after another. When the banquet began, Grandmother Jia once again told Baochai to choose. Baochai chose Lu Zhishen Makes a Drunken Uproar on Mount Wutai. Baoyu said, “You would choose this sort of play.” Baochai replied, “You have listened to operas all these years for nothing. What do you know of this piece’s merits? Its staging is excellent, and its language finer still.” “I have always disliked such noisy spectacles,” said Baoyu. Baochai laughed. “If you call this piece mere noisy spectacle, then you truly know nothing about opera. Come here, and I will tell you whether it is merely noisy or not. It is a northern suite set to Crimson Lips. Its sonorous rises and falls and its fine rhythm go without saying; but among its lyrics is an air called Parasitic Grass, whose words are extraordinarily beautiful—though of course you would never know it.” Hearing her praise it so highly, Baoyu moved closer and pleaded, “Dear sister, please recite it for me.” Baochai recited:

p.src: Idly I wipe away a hero’s tears and take leave of the recluse’s home. Thanks to your compassion, I receive the tonsure beneath the lotus throne. But lacking destined affinity, in the blink of an eye we are suddenly parted. Naked I came, and naked I go, with no ties to bind me. Where could I obtain a straw rain cape and bamboo hat to travel alone with my bundle? Let my straw sandals and broken alms bowl carry me wherever fate leads!

p.src: When Baoyu heard this, he slapped his knee and traced circles in delight, praising it without end and declaring that there was no book Baochai did not know. Lin Daiyu said, “Be quiet and watch the opera. They have not even sung The Monastery Gate yet, and already you are Acting the Madman.” Her remark made Xiangyun laugh as well. Everyone then settled down to watch the opera. When the entertainment ended that evening, Grandmother Jia had taken a great liking to the young actress playing the maiden and to one playing the clown. She had them brought in, and on looking at them closely found them more endearing still. Asked their ages, the maiden proved to be only eleven and the clown only nine, at which everyone sighed with pity. Grandmother Jia ordered some meat and fruit to be brought specially for the two children and rewarded them with two strings of cash besides. Xifeng laughed and said, “When this child is in costume, she is the very image of someone. Surely you can see whom.” Baochai knew whom she meant, but merely smiled and refused to say. Baoyu had guessed too, but he likewise dared not speak. Shi Xiangyun immediately laughed and said, “Why, she looks like Cousin Lin.” On hearing this, Baoyu hurriedly shot Xiangyun a glance and signaled to her with his eyes. But everyone had heard her. They looked closely and all burst out laughing, saying that the resemblance was indeed exact. Soon afterward, the company dispersed.

p.src: That evening, while Xiangyun was changing her clothes, she told Cuilü to open her clothes bundle, put everything in order, and pack it all up. Cuilü said, “Why the hurry? You can pack on the day you leave.” Xiangyun replied, “I am leaving first thing tomorrow morning. What is there for me to do here? Watch other people’s faces and mind their every look? What pleasure is there in that!” Hearing this, Baoyu hurried over, took her hand, and said, “Dear sister, you have misunderstood me. Cousin Lin is extremely sensitive. The others plainly knew whom Xifeng meant but would not say it, precisely because they feared she would be upset. But you blurted it out without thinking. How could she not be angry with you? I signaled only because I was afraid you would offend her. Now that you are angry with me, you have not only repaid my concern badly but wronged me as well. If it had been anyone else, what would it matter to me even if they offended ten people?” Xiangyun flung off his hand and said, “Do not try to coax me with your honeyed words. Of course I cannot compare with your Cousin Lin. Other people may talk about her and make fun of her, but the moment I say anything, I am in the wrong. I was never worthy to speak of her. She is a young mistress and master of the house, while I am only a servant girl. Heaven forbid that I should offend her!” Baoyu said anxiously, “I acted for your sake, yet somehow I have only put myself in the wrong. If I had any other motive, may I turn to ashes this instant and be trampled under ten thousand feet!” Xiangyun said, “It is the first month of the year; stop swearing and talking nonsense. Save these pointless curses, idle words, and twisted speeches for those petty, touchy people who know how to keep you under their thumb! Do not make me spit at you.” With that, she went straight into Grandmother Jia’s inner room and lay down in a fury.

p.src: Baoyu, thoroughly rebuffed, had no choice but to go and seek Daiyu. No sooner had he reached the threshold than Daiyu pushed him out and shut the door. Baoyu could not understand this either and stood outside the window, calling softly, “Dear sister.” Daiyu paid no attention to him. Baoyu lowered his head dejectedly and examined his conduct. Xiren already knew exactly what had happened and understood that persuasion was impossible at such a time. Baoyu simply stood there in a daze. Daiyu assumed that he had returned to his room and rose to open the door, only to find him still standing there. Daiyu now felt embarrassed and could hardly shut the door again, so she merely withdrew and lay down on the bed. Baoyu followed her in and asked, “Everything has a reason. If you tell me what it is, at least I will not be unjustly blamed. Everything was perfectly fine, and suddenly you became angry. What on earth caused it?” Lin Daiyu sneered. “What a fine question to ask me! I do not know the reason either. I was born for all of you to laugh at—to be compared to an actress for your amusement.” Baoyu said, “I never compared you to her, and I did not laugh. Why are you angry with me?” Daiyu replied, “You would still have to compare me yourself? You would still have to laugh yourself? You neither compared nor laughed, yet you were far worse than those who did!” Hearing this, Baoyu could find no way to defend himself and said not a word.

p.src: Daiyu went on, “I could still forgive you for that. But why did you exchange winks with Yun again? What did you mean by that? Did you suppose that if she joked with me, she would be demeaning and degrading herself? She is, after all, the daughter of a ducal and noble house, while I am merely a poor man’s maid; if she joked with me and I answered back, would she not have brought contempt upon herself? Was that not what you were thinking? That was very kind of you, to be sure; only the other one refused to appreciate your kindness and became angry too. Then you tried to please me, yet accused me of being petty and always ready to take offense. And you were afraid that if she offended me, I would be angry with her. If I am angry with her, what concern is that of yours? And if she has offended me, what concern is that of yours?”

p.src: At these words, Baoyu realized that she had overheard his private conversation with Xiangyun. On reflection, he had only tried to mediate between the two of them for fear that resentment might arise, yet not only had he failed to reconcile them, he had instead earned reproaches from both sides. It was just as he had read the other day in the Zhuangzi: “The skillful toil and the wise are troubled; the incapable seek nothing, but eat their fill and wander at ease, drifting like an unmoored boat”; and again, “The mountain tree invites its own felling, and the spring draws its own draining.” The more he thought about it, the more disheartened he became. Then he reflected further: if he could not even manage these two people satisfactorily, what could he hope to accomplish in the future? Having reached this conclusion, he saw no need to defend himself or reply, but simply turned and went back to his room. Seeing him leave, Lin Daiyu knew that reflection had made him lose heart and that he had gone off in a huff without uttering a word. This only made her angrier, and she said, “Once you go, never come back for the rest of your life, and never speak to me again.”

p.src: Baoyu ignored her, returned to his room, and lay on the bed staring blankly. Xiren knew the whole reason, but dared not address it directly, so she tried to distract him with another subject. “Today’s opera has led to several more days of performances. Miss Bao is sure to return the hospitality.” Baoyu sneered. “Whether she does or not, what business is it of anyone else?” Hearing a tone quite unlike his usual one, Xiren smiled again and asked, “Why do you say that? It is the joyous first month of the year, and all the ladies and girls are so happy together. Why have you become like this again?” Baoyu sneered. “Whether the ladies and girls are happy or not has nothing to do with me.” Xiren smiled. “If they are agreeable and you are agreeable too, would that not make things pleasant for everyone?” “What do you mean, ‘everyone’ and ‘one another’?” Baoyu said. “They may have their ‘everyone’ and ‘one another’; I came naked and unencumbered, and naked and unencumbered I shall go.” As he spoke these words, tears unconsciously began to fall. Seeing him in this state, Xiren would say no more. Baoyu pondered the meaning of those words and could not keep from bursting into sobs. p.src: When she had finished reading it, she looked over the verse as well and said with a laugh, “So this fellow has attained enlightenment. It is all my fault; that song I sang yesterday brought all this about. These Taoist writings and Chan conundrums are most apt to alter a person’s disposition. If tomorrow he begins talking these mad notions in earnest and keeps this idea in his heart, it will all have sprung from that one song of mine, and I shall be the chief culprit.” As she spoke, she tore it to shreds, handed the pieces to the maids, and said, “Burn these quickly.” Daiyu laughed. “You should not have torn it up. Let me question him. Come with me, and I guarantee I shall make him abandon these foolish and perverse notions.” The three of them accordingly went to Baoyu’s room. As soon as they entered, Daiyu said with a smile, “Baoyu, let me ask you this: that which is most precious is called ‘bao,’ and that which is most steadfast is called ‘yu.’ What is precious about you? And what is steadfast about you?” Baoyu could give no answer at all. The three girls clapped their hands and laughed. “So dull-witted, yet you would meditate on Chan!” Daiyu continued, “The closing lines of your verse—‘Nothing can be called attainment: therein lies my firm ground’—are good enough, but in my view they are not yet perfect. I shall add two more lines to it.” She then recited, “Where there is no ground on which to stand, there alone is purity.” Baochai said, “Only this can truly be called thorough enlightenment. Long ago, when Huineng, the Sixth Patriarch of the Southern School, first went in search of a master, he reached Shaozhou and heard that Hongren, the Fifth Patriarch, was at Huangmei; he therefore entered his service as the monk in charge of the kitchen fires. When the Fifth Patriarch sought an heir to the Dharma, he ordered each of his monk-disciples to compose a verse. The senior monk Shenxiu declared: ‘The body is the bodhi tree; the mind is like a bright mirror on its stand. Polish it diligently at all times, and let no dust alight.’ At the time Huineng was hulling rice in the kitchen. When he heard the verse, he said, ‘Beautiful it may be, but it has not reached ultimate understanding.’ He then composed a verse of his own: ‘Bodhi is no tree at all, nor is the bright mirror a stand. From the beginning not one thing exists—where, then, can dust alight?’ The Fifth Patriarch thereupon transmitted the robe and begging bowl to him. Today’s verse expresses the same idea. But that exchange of Chan thrusts just now has not yet been fully concluded. Surely you cannot simply let the matter drop?” Daiyu laughed. “Since he could not answer at the time, he has already lost; there would be nothing remarkable in finding an answer now. Only he must never be allowed to discuss Chan again. You neither know nor can do even what the two of us know and can do, yet you would still seek enlightenment in Chan!” Baoyu had imagined himself enlightened, but when Daiyu suddenly questioned him, he had been unable to answer, while Baochai had even cited a Chan record—abilities he had never before known either of them possessed. He reflected, “So they attained awareness before I did, yet even they have not claimed enlightenment. Why should I go looking for trouble myself?” Having thought this through, he laughed and said, “Who was seeking enlightenment in Chan? It was only a moment’s jest.” And so the four of them returned to their former easy relations.

p.src: Suddenly someone reported that Her Highness had sent out a lantern riddle for them all to guess, and had commanded each person who solved it to compose another and send it into the palace. On hearing this, the four hurried out to Grandmother Jia’s main apartments. There they saw a young eunuch holding a square, flat-topped lantern of white gauze, specially made for displaying riddles. One was already written upon it, and everyone crowded around to look and made guesses in confusion. The young eunuch further conveyed the command: “If the young ladies solve it, they are not to reveal the answer. Each must write it privately on paper, and all the answers are to be sealed together and sent into the palace, where Her Highness will judge whether they are correct.” Baochai and the others stepped forward to look. It was merely a seven-character quatrain and contained nothing especially novel. They were obliged to praise it aloud, saying how difficult it was and pretending to ponder, though in truth they had solved it at first sight. Baoyu, Daiyu, Xiangyun, and Tanchun had also solved it, and each spent some time privately writing down an answer. Jia Huan, Jia Lan, and the others were summoned as well; each racked his brains, made a guess, and wrote it on paper. Then each chose an object and made it the subject of a riddle, copied the verse in a respectful regular hand, and hung it on the lantern.

p.src: The eunuch departed and returned that evening to convey this message: “All the riddles composed earlier by Her Highness were solved, except that the Second Young Lady and the Third Young Master guessed incorrectly. Her Highness has also guessed all the riddles made by the young ladies, though whether her answers are correct is not known.” As he spoke, he brought out the written answers. Some were correct and some were not, but everyone declared at random that they were right. The eunuch also delivered the gifts bestowed upon those who had guessed correctly: each received a palace-made poem holder and a tea whisk. Only Yingchun and Jia Huan received nothing. Yingchun regarded it as a trifling amusement and paid no heed, but Jia Huan felt embarrassed and slighted. Then they heard the eunuch add, “Her Highness said the Third Young Master’s riddle made no sense and could not solve it. She told me to bring it back and ask him what it was.” At this, everyone came to see what he had composed. It read:

p.src: Seeing Yuanchun in such high spirits, Grandmother Jia grew happier still. She ordered that a small and exquisitely fashioned lantern-screen be made at once and set in the center of the main room. Each of the girls was to compose a riddle in secret, write it out, and paste it on the screen; fragrant tea, choice fruits, and all manner of trinkets were then prepared as prizes for correct guesses. After returning from court, Jia Zheng saw how delighted Grandmother Jia was; and as it was the festive season, he too came that evening to entertain her and join in the merriment. Wine and fruit were laid out, amusements were prepared, and colored lanterns were hung in the main apartments so that Grandmother Jia might admire them and enjoy herself. At the upper table sat Grandmother Jia, Jia Zheng, and Baoyu; at another below sat Lady Wang, Baochai, Daiyu, and Xiangyun; while Yingchun, Tanchun, and Xichun occupied a third. The floor was crowded with old serving women and maids. Li Gongcai and Wang Xifeng shared another table in the inner room. Not seeing Jia Lan, Jia Zheng asked, “Why is Brother Lan not here?” One of the serving women hurried into the inner room to ask Madam Li. Rising, Madam Li replied with a smile, “He said that since Master did not personally send for him just now, he would not come.” The woman reported this back to Jia Zheng. Everyone laughed and said, “He was born stubborn and contrary.” Jia Zheng promptly sent Jia Huan and two serving women to summon Jia Lan. Grandmother Jia had the boy sit beside her and handed him fruit to eat. Everyone talked, laughed, and made merry.

p.src: Ordinarily, Baoyu alone would hold forth at length, but with Jia Zheng present today, he could do no more than murmur assent. As for the others, Xiangyun, though a delicate young lady of the inner chambers, was usually fond of conversation; yet with Jia Zheng at the table today, even she kept her lips sealed. Daiyu was naturally disinclined to mix with others and had never cared to say much. Baochai was never one to speak rashly or act frivolously, and even now remained perfectly calm and composed. Thus, though this was merely an informal family gathering for amusement, everyone instead seemed constrained and ill at ease. Grandmother Jia also understood that Jia Zheng's presence alone was the cause, and after three rounds of wine she told him to go and rest. Jia Zheng understood her intention as well: once he had been sent away, the young ladies and gentlemen could enjoy themselves freely. Jia Zheng hastily smiled and said, “I heard today that Your Ladyship was holding a splendid gathering of elegant spring-lantern riddles, so I too prepared prizes and a feast and came especially to join in. Why lavish all your affection upon your grandsons and granddaughters without bestowing even the smallest share upon your son?” Grandmother Jia laughed. “With you here, none of them dares to talk or laugh, and that only leaves me bored. If you want to guess riddles, I shall give you one to solve—but if you fail, you must pay a forfeit.” Jia Zheng promptly replied with a smile, “Of course I must pay a forfeit. But if I guess correctly, I must receive a prize as well.” “Naturally,” said Grandmother Jia. Then she recited:

u.src: Jia Zheng reflected inwardly, “The firecracker composed by Her Highness is a thing that bursts once and scatters.
The abacus composed by Yingchun is struck into a tangled confusion.
The kite composed by Tanchun is a thing that drifts and floats without mooring.
The sea-lamp composed by Xichun is utterly pure, solitary, and desolate.
On this joyous Lantern Festival, why have they all made such inauspicious things the subject of their amusement?”
The more he pondered, the more oppressed he became; but in Grandmother Jia's presence he dared not let it show, and could only force himself to continue looking down the screen.
At the back he saw a regulated verse in seven-character lines, composed by Baochai, and read it aloud:

p.src: When court is dismissed, who carries smoke within both sleeves? By the zither or beneath the quilt, it has no destined place.

u.src: When court is dismissed, who carries smoke within both sleeves? By the zither or beneath the quilt, it has no destined place.

p.src: At dawn there is no need for the cock-herald to announce the watches; through the fifth watch no maid need trouble to replenish it.

u.src: At dawn there is no need for the cock-herald to announce the watches; through the fifth watch no maid need trouble to replenish it.

p.src: Morning after morning, evening after evening, the head burns with worry; day after day, year after year, the heart is consumed by anguish.

u.src: Morning after morning, evening after evening, the head burns with worry; day after day, year after year, the heart is consumed by anguish.

p.src: Time slips swiftly by and must be cherished; let wind and rain, cloud and sunshine, change as they will.

u.src: Time slips swiftly by and must be cherished; let wind and rain, cloud and sunshine, change as they will.

p.src: When Jia Zheng had finished reading, he thought to himself, “The object itself is of no great consequence. But for children so young to compose verses like these seems all the more ominous. None of them appear destined for lasting happiness or longevity.” At this thought he grew still more oppressed and looked deeply sorrowful. Eight or nine parts of his former liveliness vanished, and he merely bowed his head in brooding silence.

u.src: When Jia Zheng had finished reading, he thought to himself, “The object itself is of no great consequence.
But for children so young to compose verses like these seems all the more ominous. None of them appear destined for lasting happiness or longevity.”
At this thought he grew still more oppressed and looked deeply sorrowful. Eight or nine parts of his former liveliness vanished, and he merely bowed his head in brooding silence.

p.src: Seeing Jia Zheng in this state, Grandmother Jia reflected that he might simply be weary. She also feared that his presence would constrain the young ladies and keep them from enjoying themselves, so she said to him, “You need not guess any more. Go and rest. Let us sit a little longer, and then we too shall disperse.” At these words Jia Zheng hastily answered “Yes” several times. After reluctantly urging Grandmother Jia to take another cup of wine, he finally withdrew. Back in his room, he could do nothing but brood. Tossing and turning, he found sleep impossible and was overcome with sorrowful reflections—but of this no more need be said.

u.src: Seeing Jia Zheng in this state, Grandmother Jia reflected that he might simply be weary. She also feared that his presence would constrain the young ladies and keep them from enjoying themselves, so she said to him, “You need not guess any more. Go and rest.
Let us sit a little longer, and then we too shall disperse.”
At these words Jia Zheng hastily answered “Yes” several times. After reluctantly urging Grandmother Jia to take another cup of wine, he finally withdrew.
Back in his room, he could do nothing but brood. Tossing and turning, he found sleep impossible and was overcome with sorrowful reflections—but of this no more need be said.

p.src: Now, when Grandmother Jia saw that Jia Zheng had gone, she said, “You may all relax and enjoy yourselves.” Before she had finished speaking, Baoyu had already dashed over to the lantern before the folding screen. Gesticulating wildly, he poured out criticisms—one person’s line was poor, another’s solution did not fit—as lively as a monkey newly released from its chain. Baochai said, “Would it not be rather more refined if you sat as you did before and joined everyone in talking and laughing?” Xifeng hurried out from the inner room and cut in, “Someone like you ought to have His Lordship keep you at his side every day and never let you stray a single step. I forgot just now—why did I not urge His Lordship, right in front of him, to make you compose a verse-riddle too? If I had, I wager you would be sweating over it even now.” Her teasing put Baoyu in a fluster. He caught hold of Xifeng and clung to her, twisting and wheedling like a strand of sticky candy. Grandmother Jia chatted and laughed a while longer with Li Gongcai and the young ladies, but presently she too began to feel tired. Listening to the night watch, she heard that it was already the fourth watch. She ordered the food removed and distributed among the servants as rewards, then rose and said, “Let us go to bed. We can amuse ourselves again tomorrow evening.”
